staithe_ranger.text: Hello. You're the one who bought the Staithe lease. Thank you. I've been the warden here since before it had a warden.
It was Enclosure Ltd's until the auction. They kept it for the shooting and the tax position, in that order.

then.text: Sheep, a fence and a ditch that goes nowhere. Give it a season or two of you being cross at the drainage board and we'll see.
Sluices open. The water's coming back across the grazing and the frogs have already moved in without asking.
Listen. Low, in the reeds, like someone blowing across a bottle. That's a bittern. I've waited twenty years to say that sentence.

else.text: Cranes. Cranes, on a marsh somebody paid to drain. I shall be insufferable about this at the pub.

staithe_reeder.text: Reed's cut in winter, when the birds have gone and the ground's hard. Thatch from Norfolk reed outlasts anything imported, and I'm not at all biased.
Cut the bed on rotation and everything lives in it. Leave it alone entirely and it turns to scrub. Even nature wants a rota.
